the answers in this group collect, over every F subterm of the whole term, a size of that subterm's third argument, and claim the collection falls at every step of the context-closed relation. `KO7Benchmark.SANSTests.SubtermMeasureWitness` proves that family once, for any size satisfying two clauses: it adds one for one added S, and it does not grow when its argument is rewritten. The step rule F(x,y,S(n)) -> G(F(x,y,n)) has G unary, so each variable occurs once on each side and the rule copies nothing; the collection therefore loses one element and gains one that is smaller by one. The constructor count is a member of that family. Every rule application is a step of the same context-closed relation the theorem quantifies over, so this reading and the every-step reading are the same claim.

The step rule F(x,y,S(n)) -> G(F(x,y,n)) has G unary, so each variable occurs once on each side and the rule copies nothing; the collection therefore loses one element and gains one that is smaller by one. Read as a sum the base rule needs the discarded element to be positive, which the constructor count is on Z, so the sum falls by at least one at that rule and by exactly one at the step rule.
